smp_leg_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `purpose`; `rationale`; `reader_state_after` (`dimension: value` lines joined by line breaks, one per dimension the Leg changes); `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <entry N's holds, word for word> }` per entry of `claims` in the input, in order; and `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>"] }` per entry, in order. It carries no `introduces`. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. The Harness writes `materials` and `depends_on`.
smp_leg_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; an `introduces`; not exactly one Leg; a Claim whose `proposition` is not its entry's `holds`; a `point` or a `reader_state_after` line carrying a word of `forbidden_words`, refused naming the word and the field; and the Proof Sheet's `validateLegPathUnit` over the Leg, imported, with each entry's `material` as the text its Claim and point are recovered from. Each refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim.

sme_map_roles.note: The first Structure-Mapping Engine (kogaki#1665): one call reads the proposition into a RelationalStructure for the Persona. A second variant is a second row and a second Trial, never an edit of this one.
sme_map_roles.judgment_point: read the proposition in the input, `proposition`, as a relation among Roles. For each Role, name in one or two sentences, as its `context`, what a reader with the Persona in `persona` must come to hold, in the reader's own world, using no word of the proposition that is not a function word. Name each relation among Roles as the proposition states it, as its `holds`, again using no content word of the proposition, with `between` naming the Roles it relates. Name the one relation among those relations the proposition turns on, as `higher_order`, with `relates` naming the relations it relates and `holds` stating it in the same words of the reader's world. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_map_roles.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `strand` -- the input's `strand`, verbatim; `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "context": <one or two sentences> }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id, no Role's>, "between": [<two or more Role ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`; and `higher_order` -- `{ "relates": [<two or more relation ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`.
sme_map_roles.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or `higher_order` does not declare, or a declared key missing; an id that is empty, repeated, or names nothing; a `strand` that is not the input's; and a `context` or `holds` carrying a content word of `proposition`, refused naming the word and the field. The first refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial.

rbs_placeholder.note: The first member of the `rbs_<variant>` family of the short Trial (kogaki#1669), and NOT a ReaderBasedStrand: what the RBS is stays an open owner discussion (ruling 2026-11-04), so this row only fills the table's slot. It makes no model call: one pair per Role in the structure's order, `base` null, `target` the Role's id (kogaki#1688). A second variant is a second row and a second Trial, never an edit of this one.

rbs_base.note: The second member of the `rbs_<variant>` family (kogaki#1688): one model call chooses the base the owner chose by hand in Trials guard-reach-owner-07 and -08, under the Mapper's one-retry bound. Its answer is validated by `validateRbsTable` as the owner's file is. `rbs_placeholder` stays the default.
rbs_base.judgment_point: choose ONE domain the reader in `persona` already holds, from `persona.prior_knowledge`, in which the Roles, the relations and the higher-order relation of `structure` hold as stated. In a `holds` sentence, `{<id>}` stands for the Role of that id. Name the domain in one phrase as `base.domain`, and name its kind of match among `kinds` as `base.kind`, by the definitions given there. Then name, for EVERY Role of `structure`, in the structure's order, one base text: a noun phrase of that domain naming the object that plays the Role, written so that it reads in place of `{<id>}` in each `holds` sentence. No base text uses a content word of the proposition: the reader does not hold the Strand's words.
rbs_base.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base` -- `{ "domain": <one phrase>, "kind": <one of the `kind` values of `kinds`> }`; and `pairs` -- one `{ "base": <one noun phrase>, "target": <the Role's id> }` per Role of `structure`, in the structure's order.
rbs_base.refusal: a key the record does not declare; a `base` that is not `{ domain, kind }` or a `kind` outside the four; a pair's `base` that is not one non-empty text, or that carries a content word of the proposition, refused naming the word and `pairs[<i>].base`; a `target` naming no Role of `structure`, refused naming the id; and a Role paired other than once, refused naming the Role. The first refusal is put back into your next attempt verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `rbs`.
